title.narrative: Enhanced coverage, comprehensiveness and sustainabilty of social protection system for all workers

description.narrative: The Public Institution for Social Security (PIFSS) administers the country’s social insurance and provides only long-term benefits such as old-age, disability and death pension. While the social security benefits are too generous for nationals in the public and private sectors, a large proportion of the workforce is excluded from any type of social protection coverage whether it is in the form of social assistance or social insurance. The ILO has been collaborating for almost a decade with the Public Institution for Social Security (PIFSS) on strengthening the social security system, including periodical peer review of the actuarial valuations. This technical assistance supported the institution in developing sound actuarial practices in Kuwait and ensuring the financial sustainability of the fund. The ILO has also been engaged in carrying out actuarial valuations for the unemployment insurance scheme. Continued engagement will further focus on strengthening the social security system aiming at exploring the possibility of extending social protection coverage to those uncovered, in particular the foreign workers. End-of-Service indemnity (EOSI) benefits are one of the only social protection mechanisms in GCC countries that provide income protection to migrant workers. They are established by labour law and operate as employer-liability schemes and oblige employers to pay benefits to migrant workers when their employment ends. EOSI systems are similar across the GCC and normally pay a lump-sum gratuity, calculated as a multiple of the final wage. In this context, the ILO ROAS has produced a policy paper that draws attention to the limitations of the EOSI in GCC countries and proposes policy solutions in line with the core principles enshrined in international social security standards. This policy paper led to a dialogue, for the provision of recommendations and possible solutions/alternatives in light of international standards and best practices.
